title: Lab policy pack: initial K0823 request packet, Medicare FFS, California, Noridian Jurisdiction D

rules.title: Supported scope
rules.requirement: Every scope fact is stated explicitly and matches this pack's supported scope: Medicare FFS as primary payer, beneficiary state CA, jurisdiction Noridian JD, item code K0823, an initial request with standard handling and no accessories, an item not yet delivered, and an established, non-exempt supplier with no new enrollment or ownership change whose status interval contains the assessment date. The scope facts are the case fields payerType, payerPrimary, beneficiaryState, jurisdiction, itemCode, requestKind, urgency, accessories, alreadyDelivered, lcmpIncorporated, supplierId and supplierStatus, and the bound supplier status record they name. A stated LCMP incorporation is not a scope failure; R07 routes it to human review.

applicability.condition: Every case assessed with this pack, before any other rule's result can make it ready.

rules.basisNote: Payer process, supplier exemption and probation circumstances come from S06 and S07; the one-state, one-code, one-supplier boundary is the lab's proposed scope (SPEC Scope and R01).

sourceSections.section: Sections 4 to 7 (request contents, suppliers, power mobility devices), as summarized in docs/research.md
2026 exemption and probationary process for newly enrolled suppliers and certain ownership changes, as summarized in docs/research.md

outcomes.condition: A scope fact is stated but outside the supported scope, or stated scope facts disagree: the case supplier status differs from its bound supplier status record, the case supplierId differs from that record, the supplier status interval does not contain the assessment date (expired or not yet effective), or a bound order states an item code other than the case item code.
The supplier status record named by supplierStatusEvidenceId is access restricted (the finding names it, C07).
The supplier status record named by supplierStatusEvidenceId is unreadable (the finding names it, C07).
A scope fact is unknown (null or unknown), either supplier status interval bound is null, or no supplier status record with the ID named by supplierStatusEvidenceId is supplied.
Every scope fact is explicit, supported and consistent with its bound evidence.

rules.title: Subject binding and quarantine
rules.requirement: Every subject-scoped document is bound to the case subject: its metadata subjectId equals the case subjectId and, when its body has passed the R09 hash, parse and kind checks, a stated beneficiary identifier equals the case subjectId and a stated beneficiary name equals the case subjectName (exact string equality). A restricted or unreadable document is bound by its metadata subjectId only, and a body is never compared before its bytes are verified. A document failing any of these is quarantined: it contributes no facts, is never cited and its content appears in no finding or packet; the R02 finding names it by ID and version only (C07). Supplier status records concern no beneficiary and are not subject-scoped.

applicability.condition: Every document supplied with the case whose kind is subject-scoped (order, encounter, order receipt, supporting note), after the R09 hash, parse and kind checks and before any other rule uses its facts. A document whose metadata subjectId differs from the case is quarantined whatever its R09 result. Otherwise a document that failed provenance validation is excluded by R09 (conflict) and is not quarantined, a restricted or unreadable document is bound by metadata alone, and only an available, provenance-valid body is compared.

rules.basisNote: Proposed data-integrity requirement (SPEC R02). Comparison is exact string equality; no fuzzy name matching.

outcomes.condition: At least one subject-scoped document is quarantined. The finding cites only bound documents; the quarantined documents are listed in quarantinedDocumentIds and named in the finding by ID and version (C07).
Every subject-scoped document is bound to the case subject.

rules.title: Existing order elements
rules.requirement: A bound, usable order states: the beneficiary name or identifier, the order date, an item description, a quantity, the treating practitioner name or identifier, and signature metadata (signer name and signed date). Where either alternative is permitted, one suffices and the other is never required or invented. Signature metadata shows only that the synthetic document claims a signature; it is never reported as a verified signature.

applicability.condition: Every case; the order is an existing practitioner-authored document that the lab requests but never drafts or completes.

rules.basisNote: Standard written order elements and their name-or-identifier alternatives (S09).

sourceSections.section: Standard written order elements, as summarized in docs/research.md

outcomes.condition: More than one bound, usable, unsuperseded order exists and they state different values for an element.
The only candidate order failed provenance validation (R09 conflict; the finding names it, C07).
The only candidate order is access restricted (the finding names it, C07).
The only candidate order is unreadable (the finding names it, C07).
No bound, usable order is supplied, or the order lacks a required element (both alternatives absent where alternatives are permitted).
A bound, usable order states every required element.

rules.title: Encounter and order chronology
rules.requirement: Finalized encounter and order evidence exist, name the same treating practitioner, and the order follows completion of the encounter within six calendar months (convention C01). The lab requires an unambiguous sequence: an order dated the same day as the encounter needs review unless both sources state explicit times showing the order after encounter completion (convention C02). Completion times are never inferred from a date-only record.
rules.basisNote: Face-to-face interval, practitioner and LCMP sequencing from S08 to S10; the same-day review rule and month arithmetic are conservative lab conventions (C01, C02, C03).

rules.title: Supplier receipt of the finalized order
rules.requirement: A bound, usable supplier receipt record references the order used by R03 and R04 (document ID and version), states when the supplier received it, and that receipt time is not before the order (convention C06). Missing receipt evidence is reported without claiming that delivery occurred or did not occur. Requiring receipt evidence at packet review is a conservative lab gate.

applicability.condition: Every case, independent of whether the order itself is present; receipt evidence is assessed from receipt records only.

rules.basisNote: A written order prior to delivery is communicated to the supplier before delivery (S08, S09); making receipt a packet gate is the lab's pre-delivery choice (SPEC R05).

The only candidate receipt record is access restricted (the finding names it, C07).

rules.title: Clinical evidence stays with qualified review
rules.requirement: Clinical statements are evidence candidates for qualified review. Every case reports one case-level clinical finding that cites every clinical fact from bound, usable documents and routes them to qualified clinical review. No medical necessity conclusion follows from a diagnosis, keyword, document count or confidence, and the finding never blocks or satisfies administrative readiness. An unavailable record is not evidence that a clinical fact is absent.

applicability.condition: Every case, including one with no clinical facts.

rules.basisNote: Clinical criteria need qualified interpretation (S08); DTR separates administrative collection from clinical input (S14); the authority boundary is the lab's (SPEC R06).

sourceSections.section: Coverage criteria requiring qualified clinical interpretation, as summarized in docs/research.md

outcomes.condition: Always: clinical questions remain for qualified review whatever the administrative state.

rules.title: No generic checklist items; LCMP branch routed to review
rules.requirement: This pack imposes no assistive technology professional evaluation, specialty evaluation, home assessment or proof-of-delivery requirement on an initial K0823 packet, whatever a broad PMD checklist lists. Incorporation of an LCMP report into the encounter record is an unsupported automatic branch and is routed to human review.
rules.basisNote: Category-specific boundaries (S08), LCMP sequencing (S10), post-affirmation delivery steps and the generic scope of the PMD page and checklist (S11, S12); excluding the LCMP branch from automation is the lab's choice.

rules.title: Policy snapshot
rules.requirement: The case names this pack, the pack has a reviewed date and source provenance, and the case assessment date is one of the pack's supported assessment dates. A changed pack invalidates readiness and any prior human acceptance.

outcomes.condition: The case names a different pack, or its assessment date is not a supported assessment date.
The pack has no reviewed date or no source references.

rules.title: Source access and provenance
rules.requirement: Before any body is read, by R02 or any other rule, each document's raw bytes match its contentHash, its body parses as the structured format for its kind, and every locator resolves in that exact version. Three conditions stay distinct. Access denied (accessStatus restricted, no bytes): the document contributes no facts and rules that needed it report restricted. Content unreadable (accessStatus unreadable, a MIME type outside the pack's documentMimeTypes, or a body that is not a valid structured source): no facts, and dependent rules report unreadable. Failed provenance validation (hash mismatch, locator that does not resolve, or a body kind that differs from the metadata kind): the document is excluded (not quarantined), all its facts are excluded and dependent rules report manual_review. None of these is a negative clinical assertion. The one case-level finding takes the first matching outcome (conflict, then restricted, then unreadable) and names every affected document, whatever its condition (C07).

applicability.condition: Every document supplied with the case, checked first, before R02 compares any body. Documents that R02 quarantines (by metadata subjectId, or by a verified body naming another subject) are reported by R02 and not by R09.

rules.basisNote: Restricted data is not nonexistent data (S14); hash and locator verification is the lab's provenance rule (SPEC R09).

sourceSections.section: Restricted versus nonexistent data in documentation collection, as summarized in docs/research.md

outcomes.condition: A document not quarantined by R02 failed provenance validation: hash mismatch, a locator that does not resolve, or a body kind that differs from its metadata kind.
A document not quarantined by R02 is access restricted.

A document not quarantined by R02 is unreadable: accessStatus unreadable, a MIME type outside documentMimeTypes (text/plain is unsupported in this pack), or bytes that do not parse as the structured body for its kind.
Every document not quarantined by R02 is available, has a supported MIME type, matches its hash, parses for its kind and its locators resolve.

rules.title: Duplicate and stale action prevention
rules.requirement: Replay, restart or changed evidence never duplicates a local request or reuses a stale approval or acceptance. The durable workflow enforces this; a pure assessment of a case creates no request, approval or acceptance.

applicability.condition: Workflow actions (local requests, approvals, packet acceptance); not evaluated by a pure assessment.

rules.basisNote: Proposed workflow rule (SPEC R10), enforced by the durable workflow in a later stage.

outcomes.condition: Always for a pure assessment: no request, approval or acceptance exists to protect.

labConventions.statement: Six calendar months are added to the encounter date by calendar-month addition; when the target month is shorter, the day clamps to its last day (2026-03-31 plus six months is 2026-09-30; 2027-08-31 plus six months is 2028-02-29). The upper bound is inclusive: an order on the bound date is within the interval. This is a lab convention, not a legal interpretation.

An order dated the same day as the encounter is treated as sequenced only when both sources state explicit times (timestamp with offset) placing the order strictly after encounter completion. Date-only evidence never establishes a same-day sequence, and no time is inferred. Otherwise the case needs human review.
Practitioner sameness is compared by identifier. When the encounter or order states only a practitioner name, the lab does not decide sameness by name and routes R04 to human review.
When an LCMP report is incorporated into the encounter record, the encounter date is not used to settle chronology automatically: R04 and R07 both report manual_review.

Each rule reports exactly one finding per assessment, taking the first outcome in its list whose condition holds; outcomes are ordered so that no outcome precedes one with a higher state effect. The finding's explanation names every condition that held, not only the one that set the status. A finding cites every fact whose field is in the rule's evidenceFields, taken from bound, usable documents (not quarantined, available, of a supported MIME type and provenance-valid); facts from other documents are never cited. Usable does not imply finalized: a draft order is usable for R01, R03 and R05, and only R04 requires final status.

A receipt time (UTC) is compared with the order it references without inferring the order's time zone. The order date spans from the previous day at 10:00 UTC to the next day at 12:00 UTC across time zones. A receipt before the order's stated timestamp, or before the start of that span, is certainly before the order (conflict). A receipt within the span, when the order states no timestamp, is not sequenced (manual_review). A receipt after the span, or after the stated order timestamp, follows the order.

A finding names, by document ID and version only, the documents it concerns but cannot cite through facts (Finding documentRefs; affectedDocuments in an oracle). R02 names every quarantined document. R09 names every document not quarantined by R02 that is restricted, unreadable or failed provenance validation, whichever status it reports. R01, R03, R04 and R05 name the candidate document that set a restricted, unreadable or provenance manual_review status. A pass, missing or not_applicable finding names none, and no other rule names a document.

limitations: Authored lab subset for one synthetic scenario: initial K0823 base item, Medicare FFS primary, California, Noridian Jurisdiction D, established non-exempt supplier, assessment date 2026-10-18. It is not a complete statement of Medicare policy and has no payer endorsement.

Rules are original summaries linked to sources; no policy, checklist or questionnaire text is reproduced. Source sections are named as recorded in docs/research.md and were not reopened for this pack.
Administrative readiness only: no outcome means medical necessity, payer affirmation, payment or delivery. Clinical statements stay with qualified clinical review.
Lab conventions C01 to C07 are engineering choices for repeatable fixtures, not legal interpretations. A case that depends on an ambiguous interpretation goes to human review.
Signature metadata shows only that a synthetic document claims a signature; no signer is authenticated.

Only structured JSON source documents (application/json) are supported. The SPEC admits plain-text sources, but this pack has no plain-text extraction: a text/plain document is reported unreadable by R09 and contributes no facts.
Assessment dates other than those listed, other states, jurisdictions, item codes, request kinds and supplier circumstances need a separately reviewed pack.
